title: Congressional Award Program Reauthorization Act
official_title: To reauthorize the Congressional Award Act.
likelihoodReason: Enacted as Public Law 119-66 on December 26, 2025. Introduced by Sen. Cynthia M. Lummis (R-WY); reauthorizing an existing youth-recognition program by extending its board's termination date is a narrow measure that drew no recorded opposition, clearing both chambers before being signed.
summary: Keeps the Congressional Award Program running by pushing back the date its governing board is set to shut down. The program gives medals to young people aged 14 through 23 for achievement in public service, personal development, and physical fitness.
brief: Extends the Congressional Award Board's termination date to October 1, 2028, keeping the youth award program alive.

top_lines.headline: What the Congressional Award Program Does
subs: Awards medals to youths aged 14 through 23 nationwide
Recognizes public service, personal development, and physical/expedition fitness
Run by the Congressional Award Board, not a federal agency

top_lines.headline: What This Bill Changes
subs: Board termination date moved from Oct. 1, 2023 to Oct. 1, 2028
Extension applies retroactively as if enacted Oct. 1, 2023
Drops the fixed gold-plate/rhodium/bronze medal material requirement

items.main: Names the Act the "Congressional Award Program Reauthorization Act".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Extends the Congressional Award Board's termination date from October 1, 2023 to October 1, 2028.
items.detail: Amends Section 108 of the Congressional Award Act (2 U.S.C. 808), which sets the date the Board shall terminate. The extension takes effect retroactively as if enacted on October 1, 2023, so the Board is treated as never having lapsed. The Board administers the Congressional Award Program that awards medals to young people aged 14 through 23.

items.main: Removes the fixed material specification for Congressional Award medals.
items.detail: Amends Section 102 of the Congressional Award Act (2 U.S.C. 802). It strikes the sentence in subsection (a) requiring each medal to consist of gold-plate over bronze, rhodium over bronze, or bronze and be struck per subsection (f), and in subsection (f)(1) strikes "Subject to subsection (a), the" and inserts "The". The Secretary of the Treasury strikes the medals in such quantity, design, and specifications as the Secretary determines after consulting the Board.

underreported.summary: Strikes the statutory requirement that each medal be gold-plate over bronze, rhodium over bronze, or bronze, and removes the cross-reference tying the Treasury's striking authority to that material list.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill is captioned a reauthorization and its termination-date extension is in Section 2, but Section 3 makes a separate substantive change to what the medals must be made of rather than to the program's authorization.

gaps: The bill extends the Board's termination date to October 1, 2028 but does not itself appropriate funds or change how the program is funded.
Section 3 removes the required medal materials but does not specify any replacement material standard, leaving composition to the Secretary of the Treasury's determination.
The bill reauthorizes the Board through October 1, 2028 but sets no new standards, conditions, or oversight requirements on the program it revives.

featured_quotes.name: Mrs. Dingell
featured_quotes.text: I rise today to share my strong support for S. 284, the Congressional Award Program Reauthorization Act. Mr. Speaker, I am proud to co-lead it with my colleague, Representative Hudson, whom you just heard from, and also Congressmen Mike Levin and John Rutherford. This bill will reauthorize the Congressional Award program, which has been responsible for printing and distributing awards to young Americans across this country since 1979. This important program expired nearly 18 months ago, and it is in desperate need of reauthorization.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Hudson
featured_quotes.text: This bill simply reauthorizes the Congressional Award program, Congress' official youth recognition program and the highest honor that Congress can award our Nation's youth. This program has helped generations of young people set goals, serve others, and push themselves to achieve more. Specifically, young Americans have to set and complete rigorous personal goals focused on volunteer service, personal development, exploration, and physical fitness.

modified: Congressional Award Board termination date extended from October 1, 2023 to October 1, 2028, retroactive to October 1, 2023 (2 U.S.C. 808)

Medal material requirement changed: strikes the gold-plate-over-bronze / rhodium-over-bronze / bronze specification and the "Subject to subsection (a)" limit on the Treasury's striking authority (2 U.S.C. 802)
removed: The statutory requirement that each Congressional Award medal consist of gold-plate over bronze, rhodium over bronze, or bronze (2 U.S.C. 802(a))

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass
